tfn.s: Some parents felt the rules helped them at home.
tfn.why: The text says they "no longer had to argue alone with their children".

tfn.s: The rules will be reviewed after three years.
tfn.why: Not stated. The text does not say that the rules will be reviewed or when.

tfn.s: The writer suggests that deleting accounts does not prove that teenagers are better off.
tfn.why: The text says a platform "can point to deleted profiles without showing that anybody is better off".

tfn.s: According to the text, a national rule can ease arguments inside families.
tfn.why: The text says a national rule turns "an exhausting family argument into something closer to a fact of life".

tfn.s: The policy blocks under-16s from every messaging service.
tfn.why: The text says the opposite: "several messaging, educational and gaming services fall outside the rules."

tfn.s: Most teenagers in Australia have said they feel happier since the rules began.
tfn.why: Not stated. The text does not report what teenagers said about their happiness.

tfn.s: Changes in friendships can be measured as quickly as the removal of an account.
tfn.why: The text says long-term changes "take far longer to measure than the removal of an account".

focus.note: Check what follows the gap: a clause, a noun phrase or a new sentence. Despite takes a noun phrase, although takes a clause.

items.s: The minister's ____ that every platform would comply proved naive.

tfn.s: The writer implies that a company's total of closed accounts is not evidence that teenagers benefit.
tfn.why: The text says the large number "does not tell us whether teenagers spend less time online, move to other apps or feel any better".

tfn.s: According to the text, the 2026 research answered most questions about long-term effects.
tfn.why: The text says it left "many longer-term outcomes unresolved".

tfn.s: The eSafety Commissioner's research found that many teenagers had moved to other apps.
tfn.why: Not stated. The text only says the research offered insight into the initial implementation.

tfn.s: The writer suggests the policy would look like a failure if people expected it to end all contact with social-media content.
tfn.why: The text says a measure "judged against a promise it never made will always look like a failure", and that the policy does not outlaw every encounter.

tfn.s: The writer treats precise wording about the policy as a minor concern.
tfn.why: The text says: "Precision here is not pedantry: it determines what the policy can reasonably be expected to achieve."

speak.title: Role-play: can I keep my account?
speak.setup: Work in pairs. Read your card, then have the conversation. Swap roles and do it again.

a.text: Your 15-year-old wants to keep using a messaging app. You like the new rules because they stop the arguments at home. Ask at least two questions before you decide. You can say yes, no, or yes with a condition.

b.text: Your best friends live far away and you only talk to them on one app. Explain why it matters to you and suggest a way to use it safely.

phrases: I'd really like to stay in touch with my friends.
It's not just for fun, it's how we talk.
How much time would you spend on it?
I'm worried about what you might see.
We could try it for a month and then talk again.
That's fair, I'll agree to that.
speak.after: Afterwards, tell the class: did the parent say yes, and was it a fair decision?
